tasks.title: TRIAL 5: break the Midas terms parser on paper (30 cases, predict what the code returns)
tasks.why: TRIAL (do these first, in this order): a measured test of what this model can do; scored against answers or measurements Claude holds, not by opinion. Executing code in your head, exactly. build.py's parse_terms (line 1767) turns a card's terms bullet into purchase APR, promo APR, promo end and due day; docs/BOOK_SCHEMA.md says what it must accept. The 25 cases in test/parser_cases.json already pass. You write 30 new ones and predict, for each, what the code returns today.
tasks.unlocks: Every case where build.py disagrees with BOOK_SCHEMA.md is a real parser bug; Claude reports it to Joseph (the parser is changed only with his OK) and the case joins the test suite.
inputs: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpavia10/midas-ledger/main/build.py (parse_terms from line 1767, and the code that calls it)
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpavia10/midas-ledger/main/docs/BOOK_SCHEMA.md (what the book may say and what it means)

https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpavia10/midas-ledger/main/test/parser_cases.json and https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpavia10/midas-ledger/main/test/test_parser_cases.py (the case format and how it is run)
steps: Read parse_terms and every function it calls, and BOOK_SCHEMA.md.

Write 15 'real' cases: a terms wording a real US card issuer uses in its cardmember agreement or pricing page (cite the page, quote it under 300 characters), written as a book terms bullet. 'expect' is what BOOK_SCHEMA.md says the book means.
Write 15 'edge' cases aimed at the gaps: separators, case, spacing, dates, 0 vs missing, several rates on one line, words in a different order, deferred interest.
For every case, 'predict' is what build.py returns today, worked out from the code line by line (not what it should return), and 'why' names the lines.
Made-up numbers and names only. No real account data.

deliver.shape: JSON array of 30 objects in test/parser_cases.json's format plus kind, predict, why, source_url, quote

fields.rule: row

fields.rule: real | edge

self_check: 15 real and 15 edge.
Every real case cites an issuer's own page with a quote that is on it.
expect follows BOOK_SCHEMA.md; predict follows the code. Where they differ you have found a gap: say so in the run report.
Field names are the ones build.py writes (see the 25 existing cases).
Valid JSON, named exactly as asked.
tasks.done_when: 30 cases, each with expect, predict and why.
checks: Claude runs all 30 through build.py. Score: predictions that match the code exactly; expectations that match BOOK_SCHEMA.md; real parser gaps found (each is a bonus).
rejected_if: a prediction copied from expect without reading the code
real account data
a real case whose quote is not on the cited page
fewer than 30
tasks.review: Scored 8 (trial 5). Claude ran all 30 through build.py: 24 of 30 predictions exact; the 6 misses share one blind spot (the 'as of' date is read from the whole line, so it survives separators and labels that break the other fields). Real parser gaps found, inside what BOOK_SCHEMA.md promises: 'no deferred interest' sets deferred_interest (case 26), a non-zero promo rate beside a promo end is dropped (case 21), and three minor ones ('due 15th', 'promo' inside the due segment, 'thru' in the first promo pattern). Over-claimed: '27 of 30 real parser gaps' counts issuer wordings the book never promised to read (the book is written in the schema's own form). The issuer quotes could not be opened from Claude's machine. Gaps go to Joseph before the parser changes (protected internal).

tasks.title: 12 debt payoff cases worked to the cent
tasks.why: Midas is getting a payoff planner (avalanche, snowball and Joseph's own order). Claude checks its engine against cases worked by someone else. No real balances: every case is made up.
steps: Make 12 made-up cases: 4 avalanche, 4 snowball, 4 'custom order'. Each has 2 to 6 debts (name, balance, APR %, minimum payment) and one monthly budget at least the sum of the minimums.

Rules, exactly: each month, interest = balance x APR / 12 / 100, rounded to the cent (half up); add it to the balance; pay every minimum (or the whole balance if smaller); the rest of the budget goes to the target debt (avalanche = highest APR, snowball = lowest balance, custom = the order you list); if the target is paid off with money left, the rest goes to the next target the same month; when a debt hits 0 its minimum joins the rest from the next month.
Work every case month by month until every balance is 0.
At least 3 cases must run longer than 36 months and at least 2 must have a debt paid off in the same month another target changes.

deliver.shape: [{"case":1,"method":"avalanche","budget":900,"debts":[{"name":"Card A","balance":4210.55,"apr":24.99,"min":95}],"months":[{"m":1,"interest":{"Card A":87.68},"paid":{"Card A":900},"balance":{"Card A":3398.23}}],"payoff_month":{"Card A":6},"total_interest":312.40}] (12 objects)

tasks.done_when: 12 cases, every month listed, and Claude's engine gets the same balance for every debt in every month.
checks: Claude runs all 12 cases through its own engine; a balance more than $0.01 off in any month makes that case wrong.
Claude checks the 36-month and same-month conditions.
rejected_if: a case whose months stop before every balance is 0
a month that does not follow the rules above
fewer than 12 cases
